item.title: DP-Strong Assembly Elects 11 Committee Chairs despite Opposition's Boycott
item.description:
Photo : YONHAP News

The ruling Democratic Party(DP)-majority National Assembly has elected chairs for ten parliamentary standing committees and one special budget committee during the second half of the 22nd National Assembly during a boycott by the main opposition.

During a plenary session Tuesday, DP Rep. Seo Young-kyo was elected to lead the Legislation and Judiciary Committee; Rep. Yoo Dong-soo, the National Policy Committee; and Rep. Jo Seoung-lae, the Finance, Economy, Planning and Budget Committee.

Rep. Song Ki-hun will chair the Science, ICT, Broadcasting and Communications Committee; Rep. Jin Sung-joon, the National Defense Committee; and Rep. Kim Young-jin, the Public Administration and Security Committee.

Rep. Lee Jae-jung was elected to head the Culture, Sports and Tourism Committee; Rep. Seo Sam-seok, the Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs Committee; and Rep. Kim Jung-ho, the Climate, Energy, Environment and Labor Committee.

Floor leader Han Byung-do will oversee the House Steering Committee, and Rep. Lee Kwang-jae, the Special Committee on Budget and Accounts.

The ruling party announced candidate recommendations for eleven of 18 committee chief posts on Tuesday after failing to narrow differences with the main opposition People Power Party(PPP) over chairmanship of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee.

The PPP boycotted the plenary vote in protest, and filed a resignation document to the Assembly secretariat after speaker Cho Jeong-sik unilaterally appointed PPP lawmakers to the eleven committees.

item.title: Nat'l Team Captain Son Heung-min, Others Return Home to Fans Cheering
item.description:
Photo : YONHAP News

National football team captain Son Heung-min and several other players have returned home to cheering fans after South Korea came short of advancing to the round of 32 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Son and the other team members landed at Incheon International Airport early Wednesday.

The cheering and words of encouragement from supporters at the airport was in stark contrast to heckling by around 300 fans and YouTubers early Tuesday, when outgoing head coach Hong Myung-bo returned alongside some of the players.

Before departing from the national team’s training site in Zapopan, western Mexico, on Sunday local time, Hong apologized to the South Korean people for falling short of their expectations and announced his early resignation as head coach.

The Korea Football Association had come under scrutiny when it picked Hong as head coach for the second time in 2024, with the government and the National Assembly raising questions about transparency and fairness in the selection process.

The national team finished third in Group A with three points, results that eliminated South Korea from the eight best third-place teams that were given the chance to play in the round of 32.
